title: Come, Holy Spirit, Heavenly Dove
description: Come, Holy Spirit, Heavenly Dove in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 34, headed “Breathing after the Holy Spirit; or, Fervency of devotion desired”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, ho-ly Spirit, heav-en-ly Dove, With all thy quick-ening powers, Kin-dle a flame of sa-cred love, In these cold hearts of ours.

lines: Come, holy Spirit, heavenly Dove,
With all thy quickening powers,
Kindle a flame of sacred love,
In these cold hearts of ours.
Look, how we grovel here below,
Fond of these trifling toys;
Our souls can neither fly nor go
To reach eternal joys.
In vain we tune our formal songs,
In vain we strive to rise;
Hosannas languish on our tongues,
And our devotion dies.
Dear Lord! and shall we ever lie
At this poor dying rate?
Our love so faint, so cold to thee,
And thine to us so great?
Come holy Spirit, heavenly Dove,
With all thy quickening powers;
Come shed abroad a Saviour's love,
And that shall kindle ours.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
